title: Forth from the Dark and Stormy Sky
description: Forth from the Dark and Stormy Sky in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Reginald Heber wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 6, “The Sanctuary”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Forth from the dark and storm-y sky, Lord, to Thine al-tar's shade we fly; Forth from the world, its hope and fear, Fa-ther, we seek Thy shel-ter here: Wea-ry and weak, Thy grace we pray; Turn not, O Lord! Thy guests a-way.

lines: Forth from the dark and stormy sky,
Lord, to Thine altar's shade we fly;
Forth from the world, its hope and fear,
Father, we seek Thy shelter here:
Weary and weak, Thy grace we pray;
Turn not, O Lord! Thy guests away.
Long have we roamed in want and pain,
Long have we sought Thy rest in vain;
Wildered in doubt, in darkness lost,
Long have our souls been tempest-tost:
Low at Thy feet our sins we lay;
Turn not, O Lord! Thy guests away.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Reginald Heber died in 1826.
credits: Words by Reginald Heber (1783–1826), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
